subject.title: fix(heartbeat): skip heartbeat when session idle too long, back off after consecutive idle skips

question: Should OpenClaw accept a hardcoded default idle gate for passive scheduled heartbeats, and which heartbeat work must bypass it?
rationale: The linked spend bug is real, but the PR changes default heartbeat scheduling and delivery semantics while related tracker context still treats the durable idle policy as a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Approve a narrow safety gate
options.body: Allow a no-config seven-day guard only for plain scheduled heartbeat prompts while preserving cron, exec, wake, due-task, and commitment delivery paths.

options.title: Require configurable idle policy
options.body: Route this through the activity idle-timeout tracker so schema, docs, defaults, and upgrade behavior are decided together before changing runtime defaults.

options.title: Defer to broader safety design
options.body: Keep this PR unmerged until idle, cost, OK-only, and auth-error backoff behavior are designed as one heartbeat safety policy.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow safety gate
recommendation.body: Allow a no-config seven-day guard only for plain scheduled heartbeat prompts while preserving cron, exec, wake, due-task, and commitment delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent heartbeat runtime/docs history and prior product-review context on the linked idle-timeout tracker.
